choice.noise_with_wide_readings: CHOSEN. Real sensors are noisy; certify/16n (repeated-reading per-bit majority) exists but has only ever run on 2-bit readings at N <= 16, and every noisy 20-state attempt was Rejected in 058 because the 2-bit identifier did not decide noise-free. B4 now decides 11/12 noise-free at 20 states with budget headroom (decided records used 0.60-1.68M of 2M conflicts; Exact, RECOUNT_058), so a noisy wrapper has an identifier underneath that can decide.
choice.how_wide_is_enough: Deferred (not rejected): B3 4/12 vs B4 11/12 already brackets the threshold at this budget; more B3 seeds narrow a CI but add no new capability. Kept as next_if_fail branch and a later frontier study.
choice.larger_N_wide: Deferred: N 24/28 with 4-bit readings changes the encoding size (more state bits) and needs new budget calibration on sealed seeds first; next_if_pass candidate.
choice.single_read_flip_tolerant_encoding: Rejected for 059: an encoding that tolerates f flipped readings without re-reads is a new solver core with no pre-plan evidence; Open.

honest_framing: This is STILL A TARGET CHANGE (wide 4-bit readings). 2-bit readings at 20 states stay Open. The 059 question is only whether the existing majority front end composes with certify/20b at 20 states under iid bit flips, and at what read cost. By construction, if every majority is correct the identifier sees the noise-free trace (Exact), so the main new evidence is (a) the observed majority-error count and read cost under the anytime k rule, and (b) that the wrapper adds no unsoundness. The guarantee is conditional on the declared N (Inferred: a larger machine can copy the true machine on every visited state) and on the noise model (iid flips with eps <= eps_bar, re-reads do not move the hidden state).
brand: charcoal and sage; no purple, neon, emoji or gold
question: (A) Does brute.certify/20n (certify/16n's anytime per-bit majority rule, generalised to read_bits, on an unchanged certify/20b read_bits 4) keep B4's decision rate on fresh 20-state worlds with random 4-bit readings when each reading bit is flipped iid with eps 0.05 and 0.10? (B) How many reads per observation does it cost? (C) Is certify/20n with reads=1 on noise-free readings exactly certify/20b, and at read_bits 2 exactly certify/16n?

hypotheses.H1: no gated arm issues a WRONG certificate on 48 gated records (12 fresh seeds x 4 gated arms), ID checked from the start state and IDF from the current state against the clean truth
hypotheses.H2: N4_10 (eps 0.10, eps_bar 0.15) decides (ID+IDF) >= 6/12 and no fewer than C4 - 2 on the same seeds
hypotheses.H4: N4_10 and N4_10b give byte-identical canonical records (noise RNG seeded, conflict-counted)
hypotheses.H5: certify/20n reads=1 equals certify/20b, and certify/20n read_bits 2 equals certify/16n, record-for-record

design.api: one new module brute/api/certify20n.py (brute.certify/20n): Certifier20N(initial_reads, num_actions, family_bound, read_bits in {2,3,4}, eps_bar, delta, reads=None, ...). k rule: certify/16n reads_for with bits = read_bits (smallest odd k with read_bits*exp(-2k(1/2-eps_bar)^2) <= delta*6/(pi^2 t^2)); per-bit majority passed to an UNCHANGED certify/20b instance. certify/16n, certify/20b and earlier modules are imported only, never edited. Host-agnostic: no I/O, threads, subprocess or os.
design.worlds: experiments/worlds_059.py: for seed s, transitions, start and passive prefix exactly as worlds_058 scale20r4 for s (worlds_050 scale20 transitions; emissions rng = random.Random(s*11+580+4)). Noise: each of the k readings of observation t flips each bit independently with probability eps using rng_noise = random.Random(s*13+590+int(1000*eps)), drawn in a fixed order (t, read, bit). Re-reads do not move the hidden state.

certification_rule: certify/20n becomes certified for read_bits 4 at declared N <= 20 under iid bit noise eps <= eps_bar (eps_bar <= 0.15 tested) iff every gated criterion passes. If every gate except GN_keep59 and/or GN05_59 passes, it is published as sound but not certified. If any other gate fails it has no certification status. certify/20b, certify/16n and earlier statuses are unchanged. 2-bit 20-state worlds stay Open whatever happens.
status_wording_rule: every status phrase in RELEASE.json, README, CHANGELOG, HANDOFF, the tag message and the release notes is derived from the two GATES_059 flags: certified -> 'certified'; sound_not_certified -> 'sound but not certified'; neither -> 'not certified, no certification status' plus the failing gates

limitations: majority front end reduces noise to the noise-free problem when every majority is right; a pass is mostly composition evidence, not a new solver capability
iid flips and state-preserving re-reads are strong assumptions; correlated or state-dependent noise untested
random emissions are a modelling choice
a wide-reading pass says nothing about 2-bit 20-state worlds, which stay Open
still needs a declared size N
open_items: full N-freedom: Open (impossible from finite data without a size bound; Inferred)
IDF that fixes the start state: Open
claim_scope: conditional on the declared N and the noise model: an ID or IDF means unique among machines with at most N states consistent with the majority trace, which equals the clean trace with probability >= 1 - delta under iid flips eps <= eps_bar. Inferred reason for N: a larger machine can copy the true machine on every visited state and differ only on states the trace never reached. Never 'first decided 20-state world'. Results are for random 4-bit readings only.
